tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
- End PR bodies with:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

1	## breve descrição do objetivo
     2	
     3	Vamos montar um agente, os requisitos desse agent, dataset para testes de evaluation harness e testes no geral estão nesse repositório:
     4	
     5	* https://github.com/namastexlabs/namastex-fde-challenge
     6	
     7	nossa missão é avaliar o repositório e cumprir todos os requisitos abaixo.
     8	
     9	## requisitos técnicos
    10	
    11	* circuit breaker na chamada da tool de cotação pra evitar degradar o serviço e o downstream
    12	* retry com backoff pra falhas transitórias
    13	* não realizar retry em erros de entrada ou autorização tipo 400 401 403 e 422, avaliar separado casos tipo 429
    14	* definir timeout pras chamadas externas
    15	* fazer uma etapa de detecção/classificação de prompt injection antes da execução do agente
    16	* inputs suspeitos não podem conseguir alterar system prompts regras de negócio permissões ou comportamento das tools
    17	* regras críticas de segurança e negócio precisam estar garantidas também por código/tools e não só pela detecção de prompt injection
    18	* observabilidade das conversas e chamadas de tools
    19	* salvar trace com pelo menos:
    20	  * conversation/message id
    21	  * tool chamada
    22	  * input sanitizado
    23	  * resultado/status
    24	  * latência
    25	  * erro quando houver
    26	  * skills/regras utilizadas
    27	
    28	* avaliar langwatch ou solução equivalente pra tracing/evals
    29	* criar um catálogo de `available_skills` com descrições curtas das capacidades/regras disponíveis
    30	* o modelo deve selecionar as skills relevantes baseado na intenção da conversa e só essas regras entram no contexto
    31	* manter implementação de skills simples, podendo ser arquivo de texto/config pra evitar regra comercial espalhada no código
    32	* conversas podem chegar em raw mas antes de persistência logs ou avaliação precisam passar por sanitização e remoção de pii
    33	* não remover insultos ou conteúdo relevante da conversa durante sanitização, só dados sensíveis
    34	* usar o dataset fornecido pra análise e criação de casos de avaliação, não como fonte de verdade de preço
    35	* usar python como linguagem principal
    36	* evitar banco de dados sem necessidade real, se precisar de persistência avaliar algo simples primeiro
    37	
    38	
    39	## stack
    40	
    41	* Python + Langchain
    42	* Next.JS no frontend
    43	* Docker para subir tudo em apenas um comando simples
    44	
    45	
    46	fluxo conceitual
    47	
    48	```text
    49	user_input
    50	  -> prompt injection / safety check
    51	  -> available skills
    52	  -> skill selection
    53	  -> selected business skills
    54	  -> model
    55	  -> tool calling
    56	  -> tool result
    57	  -> model
    58	  -> response ou handoff
    59	```
    60	
    61	exemplos iniciais de skills
    62	
    63	```text
    64	quote
    65	- coleta dados necessários e realiza cotação
    66	
    67	quote_failure
    68	- define o comportamento quando a api de cotação está indisponível
    69	
    70	objection_handling
    71	- define como tratar objeções comerciais
    72	
    73	handoff
    74	- define quando encaminhar o atendimento pra um humano
    75	```
    76	
    77	as business skills devem poder definir coisas tipo
    78	
    79	* o que fazer quando a api de cotação estiver indisponível
    80	* como tratar objeções
    81	* quando realizar handoff
    82	
    83	## regras de negócio
    84	
    85	* a api de cotação é a única fonte de verdade para preços
    86	* sem uma cotação bem sucedida o agente não pode informar ou estimar preço
    87	* o agente não possui autoridade pra
    88	
    89	  * alterar preços
    90	  * conceder descontos
    91	  * criar condições comerciais
    92	  * inventar benefícios ou coberturas
    93	* ao receber uma objeção o agente deve tentar entender o motivo e responder usando só informações conhecidas sobre o produto
    94	* o objetivo ao tratar objeções é demonstrar valor e não negociar preço
    95	* quando a situação exigir negociação exceção comercial ou informação que o agente não possui fazer handoff pra atendimento humano
    96	* também fazer handoff quando
    97	
    98	  * o usuário pedir atendimento humano
    99	  * a cotação falhar definitivamente
   100	  * o caso estiver fora do escopo ou das regras disponíveis
   101	
   102	## objetivo do discovery
   103	
   104	usar o repositório do challenge e os pontos acima pra
   105	
   106	1. identificar os requisitos explícitos e implícitos do desafio
   107	2. validar quais dessas ideias realmente fazem sentido pro escopo
   108	3. evitar overengineering pra um challenge de 3 dias
   109	4. propor uma arquitetura mínima
   110	5. definir um plano de implementação priorizado
   111	6. separar claramente
   112	
   113	   * must-have
   114	   * nice-to-have
   115	   * coisas que não valem implementar no challenge
   116	
   117	não implementar nada ainda
   118	
   119	primeiro
   120	
   121	* fazer o discovery completo do repositório
   122	* confrontar essas ideias com o que o challenge realmente pede
   123	* identificar riscos e gaps
   124	* propor uma arquitetura mínima
   125	* produzir um implementation plan priorizado
   126	
   127	separar uma pasta de plano de implementação em ai_logs, onde vamos salvar os logs de ia com a seguinte estrutura:
   128	
   129	* DISCOVERY.MD
   130	* ARCHITECTURE.MD
   131	* tasks
   132	
   133	   * US-01-SUBJECT.MD
   134	
   135	* claude_logs
   136	
   137	insira HITL como wizard para me perguntar eventuais duvidas.
   138	
   139	
   140	detalhe: esse projeto está no workspace para aproveitar o devos e skills adjacentes, mas ele não pertecen ao contexto dos outros projetos.

content.content:
version: 3.0
framework: "DevOS - Agentic Workflow"

# Migrated to DevOS 2.0.0 on 2026-08-01.
# v2.0.0 REMOVED the `imports:` mechanism, so the sectional files under .devos/config/
# are no longer loaded by any workflow. Their VERIFIED values were inlined below verbatim.
# The old files are kept on disk as a reference/audit trail only — editing them has no effect.
# Pre-upgrade snapshot: .devos/memory/state/backups/pre-v2.0.0-260801.tar.gz
#
# Values here were DISCOVERED and VERIFIED against the live workspace by /devos.setup
# on 2026-07-27, not copied from the example. No credential appears in this file;
# integration auth is delegated to MCP (auth: "MCP"), inventory in .devos/mcps.json.

workspace:
  # v2 replaced the `repo_directories` list with a single parent path + explicit repo names.
  # The 3 managed repos are the ONLY entries in this directory, so the mapping is exact.
  repositories_path: "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories"
  managed_repos:
    - "cubo-workspace-app"   # Next.js 14.2 + React 18, yarn, base: staging
    - "cubo-workspace-api"   # NestJS 10 + TypeORM, yarn, base: staging
    - "cubo-app"             # Expo + React Native, npm, base: develop
  auto_fetch: true           # v2: refs only, never merges
  ignore_patterns_file: ".devos/.devosignore"

  # Legacy alias — DevOS 2.0.0 still references `workspace.repo_directories` in
  # system_prompts/planner_agent.md and workflows/metrics_workflow.md (upstream oversight).
  # Kept so those two paths keep resolving until upstream is fixed.
  repo_directories:
    - "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories/cubo-workspace-app"
    - "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories/cubo-workspace-api"
    - "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories/cubo-app"

behavior:
  verbose: false
  local_first: true
  auto_kb: true
  wizard_mode: true

skills:
  start_sources:
    - source_jira
    - source_github
    - source_meetings
    - source_local_repos
    # source_slack OMITTED deliberately: integrations.slack.enabled is false (MCP NEEDS_AUTH,
    # human deferred OAuth). Re-add it here after authenticating via /mcp, or the parallel
    # ingestion spawns a subagent that can only return empty.
  parallel_ingestion: true

digests:
  keep_history: true
  history_path: ".devos/memory/digests/"
  track_last_edited: true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KNOWLEDGE SYSTEM — inlined from config/knowledge.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
knowledge_system:
  router_enabled: true

  # Seeded by /devos.setup Step 5 on 2026-07-27. Mode: INDEX (not copy) — the notes in
  # brain_kb/ summarise assets and point at absolute source paths, so there is a single
  # source of truth. Consult .devos/memory/brain_kb/_index.yaml FIRST, then load only
  # predicate-matched entries.
  knowledge_bases:
    business_rules:
      priority: 1.2
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Domain-specific business rules, regulatory constraints, and invariants that must never be violated. Backed by FUNCIONALIDADES.md (1030 lines of pt-BR functional spec) and the workspace CLAUDE.md. Kept at the highest priority."

    github:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Repository-level knowledge: delivery conventions, branch/commit enforcement, and per-repo base-branch exceptions extracted from real git history and CI config."

    backend_architecture:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "cubo-workspace-api internals: NestJS architecture and patterns, TypeORM/database conventions, migrations, Redis cache, S3 export, transactional email (dual HubSpot/SES), and external integrations."

    mobile:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "cubo-app (Expo / React Native): branch-dependent Expo SDK major, and WSL2-specific testing constraints for Jest and Metro."

    api_contracts:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Request/response and error contracts: the external DeskBee OpenAPI 3.0 spec (52 paths) and the TICKET-XXXX day-agenda Postman collection with its typed error codes."

    jira:
      priority: 0.9
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Project management context from Jira tickets, epics, and sprint retrospectives. Project PLD on [cliente-anonimizado].atlassian.net."

    implementation_plans:
      priority: 0.8
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "38 TICKET-keyed implementation plans, test plans and smoke tests. Indexed as a collection note with a ticket->file manifest; match on the TICKET-<n> prefix. Check here before planning a ticket from scratch."

    # `kb_name_1` from the template was DROPPED — it was an unconfigured placeholder, not a domain.

  fusion:
    algorithm: weighted_rrf # Weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion — merges results across KBs respecting priority weights

  reranker:
    model: bge-reranker-large # Cross-encoder reranker applied after fusion to refine final ordering
    # Documentation of intent: fusion and reranking are performed semantically by the agent,
    # not by a loaded binary. No model is downloaded.

  retrieval:
    top_k_per_kb: 15 # Maximum chunks retrieved per knowledge base before fusion

  context:
    final_chunks: 12 # Maximum chunks injected into the working context after fusion + reranking

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INTEGRATIONS — inlined from config/integrations.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
integrations:

  jira:
    enabled: true
    auth: "MCP"                          # Auth method: MCP (via mcps.json), ENV, or TOKEN
    server: "claude.ai Atlassian"        # Live+Connected OAuth server wins over the stdio one
    base_url: "https://[cliente-anonimizado].atlassian.net"
    cloud_id: "[cloud-id-anonimizado]"
    default_project: "PLD"               # "Plataform Cubo Delivery" (id 10409). 50/50 assigned
                                         # issues are PLD, and it matches every checked-out branch.
    boards: []                           # INTENTIONALLY EMPTY — not a placeholder.
                                         # The claude.ai Atlassian MCP exposes no Agile/board tool, and its
                                         # `fetch` accepts only issue/page ARIs, so /rest/agile/1.0/board is
                                         # unreachable. Ticket discovery uses the `project = PLD` JQL path.
                                         # To populate: /devos.setup, then supply board IDs.
    filters:
      # CORRECTED from the template's ["To Do", "In Progress", "In Review"], which matched
      # 0 of 100 real PLD issues updated in the last 30 days. These are the project's actual
      # status names (partly pt-BR). Excludes In homologation / Homologated / Cancelado as
      # past the development stage.
      status:
        - "Backlog"
        - "Em andamento"
        - "Code Review"
        - "QA Test"
        - "ready for Dev Testing"
        - "Ready to QA"
      labels: []                                       # Optional: filter by labels (empty = all)
      assignee: "current_user"                         # "current_user", "unassigned", or specific ID
    lookback_days: 14                    # How far back to look for relevant tickets
    include_comments: true               # Pull ticket comments for additional context
    include_attachments: false           # Parse attached files (PDFs, images) — requires MCP support
    max_tickets: 25                      # Max tickets to retrieve per query
    # Note: the OAuth grant carries only read:jira-work / write:jira-work — no Confluence scopes.

  slack:
    enabled: false                       # Capability is NEEDS_AUTH; human deferred OAuth to a later /mcp run.
    auth: "MCP"
    server: "claude.ai Slack"
    channels: []                         # Deliberately empty rather than placeholder IDs.
    lookback_days: 7
    thread_depth: "full"                 # "full" (all replies), "top_only" (parent messages only), or integer
    include_reactions: false
    include_files: false
    max_messages_per_channel: 100
    # To enable: authenticate via /mcp, set enabled: true, and add source_slack back to skills.start_sources.

  meeting_notes:
    enabled: true                        # Enabled via the `manual` provider only — a real, working local path.
    auth: "MCP"
    providers:
      - name: "otter_ai"
        enabled: false                   # No server in any source.
      - name: "google_meet"
        enabled: false                   # CORRECTED from the template's `true`: no google-meet server is
                                         # connected. Google Drive being connected does not satisfy Meet.
      - name: "manual"                   # User drops .md files in a directory
        enabled: true
        watch_path: ".devos/memory/transcripts/"  # Verified present on disk
    lookback_days: 30
    filters:
      keywords: []
      participants: []
    max_transcripts: 10

  github:
    enabled: true
    auth: "MCP"                          # No GitHub MCP server exists; `gh` CLI is the verified fallback
                                         # (authenticated as [conta-github-anonimizada]). See pull_request.strategy.
    repositories:
      - owner: "[cliente-anonimizado]"
        repo: "cubo-workspace-app"
      - owner: "[cliente-anonimizado]"
        repo: "cubo-workspace-api"
      - owner: "[cliente-anonimizado]"
        repo: "cubo-app"
    sources:
      issues: true                       # Enabled, but note: 0 open issues across all 3 repos — this team
                                         # tracks work in Jira. Kept on in case that changes.
      pull_requests: true                # The real signal: 8 open PRs at setup time (3 / 4 / 1)
      discussions: false                 # CORRECTED from the template's `true`: has_discussions=false on all
                                         # 3 repos, so scanning it would be a guaranteed-empty call every run.
    lookback_days: 14
    max_items_per_source: 20
    # Permission ceiling: push/pull/triage granted; admin=false, maintain=false on all 3 repos.
    # DevOS can push branches and open PRs but cannot merge with override or change branch protection.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GIT — inlined from config/git.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
git:
  base_branch: "staging"                 # Target branch for PRs — MAJORITY value only.
  # [WARNING] The managed repos DISAGREE and this key is single-valued:
  #   cubo-workspace-app -> staging     (also has `production`)
  #   cubo-workspace-api -> staging     (also has `production`)
  #   cubo-app           -> develop     <-- EXCEPTION
  # Verified against both local origin/HEAD and `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> .default_branch`.
  # Opening a cubo-app PR against `staging` WILL fail — that branch does not exist on its remote.
  # The exception is recorded at severity: critical in
  # .devos/memory/brain_kb/base-branch-per-repo.md; the dev workflow must resolve the base per repo.
  base_branch_overrides:                 # Non-template key: makes the exception machine-readable
    cubo-app: "develop"

  branch_naming: "<type>/<jira_key>/<short_slug>"
  # Available tokens: <type>, <jira_key>, <short_slug>, <date>
  # Example output: feature/TICKET-XXXX/endpoint-agenda-do-dia-sala
  #
  # Derived from 54 real branches, replacing the template's `devos/<type>/<jira_key>-<short_slug>`.
  # The `devos/` prefix was deliberately DROPPED so DevOS branches are indistinguishable from
  # hand-made ones and match the same CI path filters.
  # Observed variance (informational): cubo-app often uses `feat/` rather than `feature/`, and
  # sometimes hyphenates the key (feat/TICKET-XXXX-onboarding-primeiro-acesso) instead of the slash form.
  # Placeholder keys TICKET-XXXX / TICKET-XXXX / TICKET-XXXX are used for unticketed work — a direct
  # consequence of commitlint's `scope-empty: never` rule.

  commit_format: "conventional"          # "conventional" (feat:, fix:, etc.), "angular", or "freeform"
  commit_scope_from: "jira_key"          # MANDATORY, not a preference — see below.
  commit_language: "pt-BR"               # Real commit subjects are Portuguese; generated commits should match.
  # Commit messages are MACHINE-ENFORCED by a husky `commit-msg` hook running commitlint:
  #   shape:      <type>(<JIRA-KEY>): <lowercase subject, no trailing period>
  #   type-enum:  feat fix perf revert refactor docs test chore build ci
  #   rules:      scope-empty: never  +  custom scope-jira-pattern /^[A-Z]+-\d+$/
  #               subject-case: never upper/pascal/start-case; subject-full-stop: never '.'
  # [WARNING] cubo-workspace-app does NOT actually enforce the Jira-scope rule: it ships both
  # .commitlintrc.js (bare config-conventional) and commitlint.config.js (full rules), and the
  # former shadows the latter. Verified by executing commitlint in both repos — a scope-less
  # message PASSES in the app repo and FAILS in the api repo. Always emit the strict form; it is
  # valid in both. See brain_kb/commit-convention-enforcement.md.

  auto_stage: true                       # Safe here: pre-commit hooks run lint / lint-staged
  sign_commits: false                    # commit.gpgsign is unset globally and per-repo

  protected_branches:                    # Non-template key: husky pre-push already blocks these
    - "main"
    - "develop"
    - "staging"
    - "production"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VERIFICATION — inlined from config/verification.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
verification:
  # POLICY, NOT COMMANDS. The `verify` skill discovers the actual command per project by reading
  # that project's manifest at run time. Do not add `command:` keys here.
  #
  # Command discovery observed at setup (informational — 2026-07-27):
  #   cubo-workspace-app  build=yarn build(next)  lint=yarn lint  type=yarn type-check(tsc)  test=vitest  cov=test:coverage
  #   cubo-workspace-api  build=yarn build(nest)  lint=yarn lint  type=(none)                test=jest    cov=test:cov
  #   cubo-app            build=(none, EAS)       lint=expo lint  type=(none)                test=jest    cov=test:coverage

  max_loop_iterations: 5                 # Max fix-verify cycles before escalating to human

  build:
    enabled: true                        # Present in 2 of 3 repos.
    # cubo-app has NO build script (Expo builds via EAS, not locally). The verify skill must SKIP
    # this gate for cubo-app rather than fail it. The api's husky pre-push already runs `npm run build`.
    timeout_seconds: 120
    max_retries: 2

  lint:
    enabled: true                        # Present in all 3 repos
    auto_fix: true                       # Attempt auto-fix before reporting errors (api has lint:fix)
    fail_on_warnings: false

  tests:
    enabled: true
    coverage:
      enabled: true                      # A coverage script exists in all 3 repos
      threshold: 90                      # RAISED from the template's 80.
      fail_below_threshold: false        # ...but ADVISORY, deliberately.
      # Reasoning: cubo-app/jest.config.js already HARD-ENFORCES
      #   coverageThreshold.global = {branches:90, functions:90, lines:90, statements:90}
      # scoped to src/features/auth/** and src/features/onboarding/**. A DevOS policy of 80 would be
      # meaningless there — jest fails the run at 89% before DevOS evaluates anything. Meanwhile
      # cubo-workspace-app and cubo-workspace-api configure NO coverageThreshold at all, so their real
      # baseline is unmeasured; hard-failing them at 90 would block every run on an unknown.
      # So: align the number to the strictest repo that actually enforces one, but keep DevOS's own
      # gate advisory until a measured baseline exists. Repo-local config remains binding either way.
      # Flip fail_below_threshold to true once baselines are known.
    timeout_seconds: 300
    must_pass: true

  type_check:
    enabled: true                        # CHANGED from the template's `false`.
    # All three repos have a tsconfig.json. Only cubo-workspace-app defines a `type-check` script,
    # so verification should fall back to `npx tsc --noEmit` in the api and in cubo-app.

  documentation:
    enabled: true
    auto_update: true
    files:                               # Pruned to files that actually exist in the selected repos
      - path: "README.md"
        rule: "Ensure README reflects any new features, changed APIs, or updated setup instructions."
      - path: "CLAUDE.md"
        rule: "Update project-level AI instructions if new modules, conventions, or gotchas were introduced. Present in cubo-app (which delegates to AGENTS.md) and at the workspace root."
      - path: "AGENTS.md"
        rule: "Added at setup: this is the real agent-instruction file in cubo-app. Keep its stated Expo SDK target consistent with the branch's package.json — see brain_kb/expo-sdk-version-drift.md."
    # DROPPED from the template, with reasons:
    #   CHANGELOG.md  -> generated by semantic-release in cubo-workspace-app and cubo-workspace-api;
    #                    hand-appending a "Keep a Changelog" entry would conflict with the generated
    #                    file and be overwritten on the next release. Absent in cubo-app.
    #                    See brain_kb/changelog-is-generated.md. DO NOT EDIT.
    #   docs/agents.md -> does not exist in any selected repo.
    #   API.md         -> does not exist; the API documents itself under docs/ instead.
    commit_message: "docs(<scope>): update documentation to reflect recent changes"
    # NOTE: this scope must be a Jira key (e.g. `docs(TICKET-XXXX):`) or the commit-msg hook rejects it
    # in cubo-workspace-api. See brain_kb/commit-convention-enforcement.md.

  instrumentation:
    enabled: true
    checks:
      - name: "logging"
        rule: "All new public functions and API endpoints must include structured logging (entry, exit, error)."
      - name: "error_handling"
        rule: "All async operations must have explicit error handling. No unhandled promise rejections. Errors must be logged with context before propagating."
      - name: "metrics"
        rule: "Key business operations must emit counters or histograms. Verify metric names follow naming conventions."
      - name: "tracing"
        rule: "RETAINED and scoped: cubo-workspace-api genuinely spans service boundaries (Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, CloudWatch), so propagate spans and add new ones for significant operations there. Treat as N/A for cubo-app, which has no distributed services."
      - name: "security"
        rule: "No secrets in code. No SQL concatenation. Inputs validated at boundary. Auth checks on protected endpoints."
      # Added at setup, both evidence-based rather than speculative:
      - name: "accessibility"
        rule: "Frontend changes (cubo-workspace-app, cubo-app) must preserve semantics and keyboard/screen-reader behaviour: correct ARIA roles and aria-current, focus visibility, and labels on interactive elements. This repo has real a11y history (feature/TICKET-XXXX/aria-current-events-calendar)."
      - name: "migration_safety"
        rule: "Any cubo-workspace-api schema change must ship a reversible TypeORM migration created under scripts/migrations (NOT the default path), must not drop or rename a column in the same release that stops writing it, and must be safe to run against a populated database. See docs/migrations.md."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PULL REQUEST — inlined from config/pull_request.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
pull_request:
  auto_create: true
  strategy: "gh_cli"                     # RESOLVED CONCRETELY at setup, not left as "auto".
  # Resolution trace:
  #   1. MCP GitHub/GitLab server enabled in mcps.json?  -> NO (none exists in any source)
  #   2. `gh` CLI installed and authenticated?           -> YES ([conta-github-anonimizada], ssh, scopes
  #                                                             repo/read:org/gist/admin:public_key)
  #   3. `glab` CLI?                                     -> not installed (all remotes are github.com)
  #   4. local_compare fallback                          -> not needed
  # Permission ceiling: push/pull/triage on all 3 repos, admin=false / maintain=false. DevOS can
  # push branches and open PRs but CANNOT merge with override. Every PR needs a human or CI approver.

  draft: false
  base_branch: "staging"                 # See git — cubo-app is an exception and targets `develop`.
                                         # Resolve per repo via git.base_branch_overrides.
  title_template: "[<jira_key>] <title>"
  body_sections:
    - "summary"
    - "changes_made"
    - "implementation_plan"
    - "testing_done"
    - "instrumentation_checklist"
    - "documentation_updates"
    - "knowledge_brief_excerpt"
    - "jira_link"
  reviewers: []                          # No CODEOWNERS-derived default detected
  team_reviewers: []
  labels: ["devos-generated"]
  link_jira: true

  jira_transition_on_pr: "To code review"
  jira_transition_id: "13"
  # CORRECTED from the template's "In Review", which DOES NOT EXIST in this Jira workflow and would
  # have failed silently at PR time.
  # Validated live via getTransitionsForJiraIssue: transition id 13, name "To code review",
  # target status "Code Review" (id 10791, category "Em andamento").
  # [CORRECTED 2026-09-01, TICKET-XXXX] The earlier note here claimed transition 13 was unreachable
  # from "Backlog" because isGlobal is false. That inference was wrong: isGlobal only means the
  # transition is not offered from EVERY status, not that Backlog is excluded. Verified live —
  # getTransitionsForJiraIssue on TICKET-XXXX (status "Backlog") listed id 13 with isAvailable: true,
  # and the transition succeeded straight to "Code Review". Keep tolerating an unavailable
  # transition, but do not skip it preemptively for a Backlog ticket: ASK Jira, do not infer.
  # Full transition set observed: Caixa de entrada(2), Backlog(4), Cancelled(6), Blocked(7),
  # Priorizado(15), Análise e refinamento(16), ready for Dev Testing(14), Return to backlog(12),
  # To code review(13).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PATHS — v2 added `skills` and `digests`
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
paths:
  prompts: ".devos/system_prompts/"
  workflows: ".devos/workflows/"
  skills: ".devos/skills/"
  state: ".devos/memory/state/"
  digests: ".devos/memory/digests/"
  brain_kb: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
  transcripts: ".devos/memory/transcripts/"
  metrics: ".devos/memory/metrics/"
  scripts: ".devos/scripts/"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Setup / upgrade provenance — what was decided and what remains open.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
setup:
  last_run: "2026-07-27"
  mode: "bootstrap"
  state_artifact: ".devos/memory/state/setup_260727.md"
  upgraded_to: "2.0.0"
  upgraded_on: "2026-08-01"
  upgrade_backup: ".devos/memory/state/backups/pre-v2.0.0-260801.tar.gz"
  known_risks:
    # Human declined the fix on 2026-07-27; carried as an accepted risk, not dropped.
    # STILL PRESENT in upstream v2.0.0 — the shipped .gitignore is byte-identical UTF-16LE.
    - id: "gitignore-utf16"
      detail: >-
        .gitignore is UTF-16LE with a BOM, so git cannot parse it and ALL of its rules are dead
        (verified by reproducing in a scratch repo). .devos/memory/state|transcripts|metrics are
        therefore not ignored, and neither config.yaml nor mcps.json is listed at all.
        Latent while this workspace is not a git repository and no secrets are stored in either file.
        Becomes live the moment either changes. Upstream fix recommended in BrunoBNascimento/devos.
      accepted_by_human: true
    - id: "v2-stale-repo-directories"
      detail: >-
        DevOS 2.0.0 removed workspace.repo_directories from the schema but still reads it in
        system_prompts/planner_agent.md and workflows/metrics_workflow.md. The key is retained
        above as a legacy alias so both keep working. Remove once upstream migrates them.
      accepted_by_human: false
    - id: "v2-setup-workflow-config-dir"
      detail: >-
        DevOS 2.0.0 setup_workflow.md still writes .devos/config/integrations.yaml,
        .devos/config/verification.yaml and .devos/config/state.json, which nothing reads
        (imports: was removed). Re-running /devos.setup may write there instead of into this file.
        Verify config.yaml after any future setup run.
      accepted_by_human: false
  follow_ups:
    - "Rotate the plaintext [VARIAVEL_TOKEN] in /home/bruno_benicio/projects/.mcp.json (superseded by OAuth; prefer deleting the stdio entry)."
    - "Authenticate the remaining MCP servers interactively via /mcp (human deferred during setup) — Slack in particular, to re-enable source_slack."
    - "Delete cubo-workspace-app/.commitlintrc.js so its intended Jira-scope rule takes effect."
    - "Decide whether cubo-app's Expo 54 downgrade merges back into develop (currently 56)."

version: 3.0
framework: "DevOS - Agentic Workflow"

# Migrated to DevOS 2.0.0 on 2026-08-01.
# v2.0.0 REMOVED the `imports:` mechanism, so the sectional files under .devos/config/
# are no longer loaded by any workflow. Their VERIFIED values were inlined below verbatim.
# The old files are kept on disk as a reference/audit trail only — editing them has no effect.
# Pre-upgrade snapshot: .devos/memory/state/backups/pre-v2.0.0-260801.tar.gz
#
# Values here were DISCOVERED and VERIFIED against the live workspace by /devos.setup
# on 2026-07-27, not copied from the example. No credential appears in this file;
# integration auth is delegated to MCP (auth: "MCP"), inventory in .devos/mcps.json.

workspace:
  # v2 replaced the `repo_directories` list with a single parent path + explicit repo names.
  # The 3 managed repos are the ONLY entries in this directory, so the mapping is exact.
  repositories_path: "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories"
  managed_repos:
    - "cubo-workspace-app"   # Next.js 14.2 + React 18, yarn, base: staging
    - "cubo-workspace-api"   # NestJS 10 + TypeORM, yarn, base: staging
    - "cubo-app"             # Expo + React Native, npm, base: develop
  auto_fetch: true           # v2: refs only, never merges
  ignore_patterns_file: ".devos/.devosignore"

  # Legacy alias — DevOS 2.0.0 still references `workspace.repo_directories` in
  # system_prompts/planner_agent.md and workflows/metrics_workflow.md (upstream oversight).
  # Kept so those two paths keep resolving until upstream is fixed.
  repo_directories:
    - "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories/cubo-workspace-app"
    - "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories/cubo-workspace-api"
    - "/home/bruno_benicio/projects/repositories/cubo-app"

behavior:
  verbose: false
  local_first: true
  auto_kb: true
  wizard_mode: true

skills:
  start_sources:
    - source_jira
    - source_github
    - source_meetings
    - source_local_repos
    # source_slack OMITTED deliberately: integrations.slack.enabled is false (MCP NEEDS_AUTH,
    # human deferred OAuth). Re-add it here after authenticating via /mcp, or the parallel
    # ingestion spawns a subagent that can only return empty.
  parallel_ingestion: true

digests:
  keep_history: true
  history_path: ".devos/memory/digests/"
  track_last_edited: true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# KNOWLEDGE SYSTEM — inlined from config/knowledge.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
knowledge_system:
  router_enabled: true

  # Seeded by /devos.setup Step 5 on 2026-07-27. Mode: INDEX (not copy) — the notes in
  # brain_kb/ summarise assets and point at absolute source paths, so there is a single
  # source of truth. Consult .devos/memory/brain_kb/_index.yaml FIRST, then load only
  # predicate-matched entries.
  knowledge_bases:
    business_rules:
      priority: 1.2
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Domain-specific business rules, regulatory constraints, and invariants that must never be violated. Backed by FUNCIONALIDADES.md (1030 lines of pt-BR functional spec) and the workspace CLAUDE.md. Kept at the highest priority."

    github:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Repository-level knowledge: delivery conventions, branch/commit enforcement, and per-repo base-branch exceptions extracted from real git history and CI config."

    backend_architecture:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "cubo-workspace-api internals: NestJS architecture and patterns, TypeORM/database conventions, migrations, Redis cache, S3 export, transactional email (dual HubSpot/SES), and external integrations."

    mobile:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "cubo-app (Expo / React Native): branch-dependent Expo SDK major, and WSL2-specific testing constraints for Jest and Metro."

    api_contracts:
      priority: 1.0
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Request/response and error contracts: the external DeskBee OpenAPI 3.0 spec (52 paths) and the TICKET-XXXX day-agenda Postman collection with its typed error codes."

    jira:
      priority: 0.9
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "Project management context from Jira tickets, epics, and sprint retrospectives. Project PLD on [cliente-anonimizado].atlassian.net."

    implementation_plans:
      priority: 0.8
      path: ".devos/memory/brain_kb/"
      description: "38 TICKET-keyed implementation plans, test plans and smoke tests. Indexed as a collection note with a ticket->file manifest; match on the TICKET-<n> prefix. Check here before planning a ticket from scratch."

    # `kb_name_1` from the template was DROPPED — it was an unconfigured placeholder, not a domain.

  fusion:
    algorithm: weighted_rrf # Weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion — merges results across KBs respecting priority weights

  reranker:
    model: bge-reranker-large # Cross-encoder reranker applied after fusion to refine final ordering
    # Documentation of intent: fusion and reranking are performed semantically by the agent,
    # not by a loaded binary. No model is downloaded.

  retrieval:
    top_k_per_kb: 15 # Maximum chunks retrieved per knowledge base before fusion

  context:
    final_chunks: 12 # Maximum chunks injected into the working context after fusion + reranking

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INTEGRATIONS — inlined from config/integrations.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
integrations:

  jira:
    enabled: true
    auth: "MCP"                          # Auth method: MCP (via mcps.json), ENV, or TOKEN
    server: "claude.ai Atlassian"        # Live+Connected OAuth server wins over the stdio one
    base_url: "https://[cliente-anonimizado].atlassian.net"
    cloud_id: "[cloud-id-anonimizado]"
    default_project: "PLD"               # "Plataform Cubo Delivery" (id 10409). 50/50 assigned
                                         # issues are PLD, and it matches every checked-out branch.
    boards: []                           # INTENTIONALLY EMPTY — not a placeholder.
                                         # The claude.ai Atlassian MCP exposes no Agile/board tool, and its
                                         # `fetch` accepts only issue/page ARIs, so /rest/agile/1.0/board is
                                         # unreachable. Ticket discovery uses the `project = PLD` JQL path.
                                         # To populate: /devos.setup, then supply board IDs.
    filters:
      # CORRECTED from the template's ["To Do", "In Progress", "In Review"], which matched
      # 0 of 100 real PLD issues updated in the last 30 days. These are the project's actual
      # status names (partly pt-BR). Excludes In homologation / Homologated / Cancelado as
      # past the development stage.
      status:
        - "Backlog"
        - "Em andamento"
        - "Code Review"
        - "QA Test"
        - "ready for Dev Testing"
        - "Ready to QA"
      labels: []                                       # Optional: filter by labels (empty = all)
      assignee: "current_user"                         # "current_user", "unassigned", or specific ID
    lookback_days: 14                    # How far back to look for relevant tickets
    include_comments: true               # Pull ticket comments for additional context
    include_attachments: false           # Parse attached files (PDFs, images) — requires MCP support
    max_tickets: 25                      # Max tickets to retrieve per query
    # Note: the OAuth grant carries only read:jira-work / write:jira-work — no Confluence scopes.

  slack:
    enabled: false                       # Capability is NEEDS_AUTH; human deferred OAuth to a later /mcp run.
    auth: "MCP"
    server: "claude.ai Slack"
    channels: []                         # Deliberately empty rather than placeholder IDs.
    lookback_days: 7
    thread_depth: "full"                 # "full" (all replies), "top_only" (parent messages only), or integer
    include_reactions: false
    include_files: false
    max_messages_per_channel: 100
    # To enable: authenticate via /mcp, set enabled: true, and add source_slack back to skills.start_sources.

  meeting_notes:
    enabled: true                        # Enabled via the `manual` provider only — a real, working local path.
    auth: "MCP"
    providers:
      - name: "otter_ai"
        enabled: false                   # No server in any source.
      - name: "google_meet"
        enabled: false                   # CORRECTED from the template's `true`: no google-meet server is
                                         # connected. Google Drive being connected does not satisfy Meet.
      - name: "manual"                   # User drops .md files in a directory
        enabled: true
        watch_path: ".devos/memory/transcripts/"  # Verified present on disk
    lookback_days: 30
    filters:
      keywords: []
      participants: []
    max_transcripts: 10

  github:
    enabled: true
    auth: "MCP"                          # No GitHub MCP server exists; `gh` CLI is the verified fallback
                                         # (authenticated as [conta-github-anonimizada]). See pull_request.strategy.
    repositories:
      - owner: "[cliente-anonimizado]"
        repo: "cubo-workspace-app"
      - owner: "[cliente-anonimizado]"
        repo: "cubo-workspace-api"
      - owner: "[cliente-anonimizado]"
        repo: "cubo-app"
    sources:
      issues: true                       # Enabled, but note: 0 open issues across all 3 repos — this team
                                         # tracks work in Jira. Kept on in case that changes.
      pull_requests: true                # The real signal: 8 open PRs at setup time (3 / 4 / 1)
      discussions: false                 # CORRECTED from the template's `true`: has_discussions=false on all
                                         # 3 repos, so scanning it would be a guaranteed-empty call every run.
    lookback_days: 14
    max_items_per_source: 20
    # Permission ceiling: push/pull/triage granted; admin=false, maintain=false on all 3 repos.
    # DevOS can push branches and open PRs but cannot merge with override or change branch protection.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GIT — inlined from config/git.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
git:
  base_branch: "staging"                 # Target branch for PRs — MAJORITY value only.
  # [WARNING] The managed repos DISAGREE and this key is single-valued:
  #   cubo-workspace-app -> staging     (also has `production`)
  #   cubo-workspace-api -> staging     (also has `production`)
  #   cubo-app           -> develop     <-- EXCEPTION
  # Verified against both local origin/HEAD and `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo> .default_branch`.
  # Opening a cubo-app PR against `staging` WILL fail — that branch does not exist on its remote.
  # The exception is recorded at severity: critical in
  # .devos/memory/brain_kb/base-branch-per-repo.md; the dev workflow must resolve the base per repo.
  base_branch_overrides:                 # Non-template key: makes the exception machine-readable
    cubo-app: "develop"

  branch_naming: "<type>/<jira_key>/<short_slug>"
  # Available tokens: <type>, <jira_key>, <short_slug>, <date>
  # Example output: feature/TICKET-XXXX/endpoint-agenda-do-dia-sala
  #
  # Derived from 54 real branches, replacing the template's `devos/<type>/<jira_key>-<short_slug>`.
  # The `devos/` prefix was deliberately DROPPED so DevOS branches are indistinguishable from
  # hand-made ones and match the same CI path filters.
  # Observed variance (informational): cubo-app often uses `feat/` rather than `feature/`, and
  # sometimes hyphenates the key (feat/TICKET-XXXX-onboarding-primeiro-acesso) instead of the slash form.
  # Placeholder keys TICKET-XXXX / TICKET-XXXX / TICKET-XXXX are used for unticketed work — a direct
  # consequence of commitlint's `scope-empty: never` rule.

  commit_format: "conventional"          # "conventional" (feat:, fix:, etc.), "angular", or "freeform"
  commit_scope_from: "jira_key"          # MANDATORY, not a preference — see below.
  commit_language: "pt-BR"               # Real commit subjects are Portuguese; generated commits should match.
  # Commit messages are MACHINE-ENFORCED by a husky `commit-msg` hook running commitlint:
  #   shape:      <type>(<JIRA-KEY>): <lowercase subject, no trailing period>
  #   type-enum:  feat fix perf revert refactor docs test chore build ci
  #   rules:      scope-empty: never  +  custom scope-jira-pattern /^[A-Z]+-\d+$/
  #               subject-case: never upper/pascal/start-case; subject-full-stop: never '.'
  # [WARNING] cubo-workspace-app does NOT actually enforce the Jira-scope rule: it ships both
  # .commitlintrc.js (bare config-conventional) and commitlint.config.js (full rules), and the
  # former shadows the latter. Verified by executing commitlint in both repos — a scope-less
  # message PASSES in the app repo and FAILS in the api repo. Always emit the strict form; it is
  # valid in both. See brain_kb/commit-convention-enforcement.md.

  auto_stage: true                       # Safe here: pre-commit hooks run lint / lint-staged
  sign_commits: false                    # commit.gpgsign is unset globally and per-repo

  protected_branches:                    # Non-template key: husky pre-push already blocks these
    - "main"
    - "develop"
    - "staging"
    - "production"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VERIFICATION — inlined from config/verification.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
verification:
  # POLICY, NOT COMMANDS. The `verify` skill discovers the actual command per project by reading
  # that project's manifest at run time. Do not add `command:` keys here.
  #
  # Command discovery observed at setup (informational — 2026-07-27):
  #   cubo-workspace-app  build=yarn build(next)  lint=yarn lint  type=yarn type-check(tsc)  test=vitest  cov=test:coverage
  #   cubo-workspace-api  build=yarn build(nest)  lint=yarn lint  type=(none)                test=jest    cov=test:cov
  #   cubo-app            build=(none, EAS)       lint=expo lint  type=(none)                test=jest    cov=test:coverage

  max_loop_iterations: 5                 # Max fix-verify cycles before escalating to human

  build:
    enabled: true                        # Present in 2 of 3 repos.
    # cubo-app has NO build script (Expo builds via EAS, not locally). The verify skill must SKIP
    # this gate for cubo-app rather than fail it. The api's husky pre-push already runs `npm run build`.
    timeout_seconds: 120
    max_retries: 2

  lint:
    enabled: true                        # Present in all 3 repos
    auto_fix: true                       # Attempt auto-fix before reporting errors (api has lint:fix)
    fail_on_warnings: false

  tests:
    enabled: true
    coverage:
      enabled: true                      # A coverage script exists in all 3 repos
      threshold: 90                      # RAISED from the template's 80.
      fail_below_threshold: false        # ...but ADVISORY, deliberately.
      # Reasoning: cubo-app/jest.config.js already HARD-ENFORCES
      #   coverageThreshold.global = {branches:90, functions:90, lines:90, statements:90}
      # scoped to src/features/auth/** and src/features/onboarding/**. A DevOS policy of 80 would be
      # meaningless there — jest fails the run at 89% before DevOS evaluates anything. Meanwhile
      # cubo-workspace-app and cubo-workspace-api configure NO coverageThreshold at all, so their real
      # baseline is unmeasured; hard-failing them at 90 would block every run on an unknown.
      # So: align the number to the strictest repo that actually enforces one, but keep DevOS's own
      # gate advisory until a measured baseline exists. Repo-local config remains binding either way.
      # Flip fail_below_threshold to true once baselines are known.
    timeout_seconds: 300
    must_pass: true

  type_check:
    enabled: true                        # CHANGED from the template's `false`.
    # All three repos have a tsconfig.json. Only cubo-workspace-app defines a `type-check` script,
    # so verification should fall back to `npx tsc --noEmit` in the api and in cubo-app.

  documentation:
    enabled: true
    auto_update: true
    files:                               # Pruned to files that actually exist in the selected repos
      - path: "README.md"
        rule: "Ensure README reflects any new features, changed APIs, or updated setup instructions."
      - path: "CLAUDE.md"
        rule: "Update project-level AI instructions if new modules, conventions, or gotchas were introduced. Present in cubo-app (which delegates to AGENTS.md) and at the workspace root."
      - path: "AGENTS.md"
        rule: "Added at setup: this is the real agent-instruction file in cubo-app. Keep its stated Expo SDK target consistent with the branch's package.json — see brain_kb/expo-sdk-version-drift.md."
    # DROPPED from the template, with reasons:
    #   CHANGELOG.md  -> generated by semantic-release in cubo-workspace-app and cubo-workspace-api;
    #                    hand-appending a "Keep a Changelog" entry would conflict with the generated
    #                    file and be overwritten on the next release. Absent in cubo-app.
    #                    See brain_kb/changelog-is-generated.md. DO NOT EDIT.
    #   docs/agents.md -> does not exist in any selected repo.
    #   API.md         -> does not exist; the API documents itself under docs/ instead.
    commit_message: "docs(<scope>): update documentation to reflect recent changes"
    # NOTE: this scope must be a Jira key (e.g. `docs(TICKET-XXXX):`) or the commit-msg hook rejects it
    # in cubo-workspace-api. See brain_kb/commit-convention-enforcement.md.

  instrumentation:
    enabled: true
    checks:
      - name: "logging"
        rule: "All new public functions and API endpoints must include structured logging (entry, exit, error)."
      - name: "error_handling"
        rule: "All async operations must have explicit error handling. No unhandled promise rejections. Errors must be logged with context before propagating."
      - name: "metrics"
        rule: "Key business operations must emit counters or histograms. Verify metric names follow naming conventions."
      - name: "tracing"
        rule: "RETAINED and scoped: cubo-workspace-api genuinely spans service boundaries (Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, CloudWatch), so propagate spans and add new ones for significant operations there. Treat as N/A for cubo-app, which has no distributed services."
      - name: "security"
        rule: "No secrets in code. No SQL concatenation. Inputs validated at boundary. Auth checks on protected endpoints."
      # Added at setup, both evidence-based rather than speculative:
      - name: "accessibility"
        rule: "Frontend changes (cubo-workspace-app, cubo-app) must preserve semantics and keyboard/screen-reader behaviour: correct ARIA roles and aria-current, focus visibility, and labels on interactive elements. This repo has real a11y history (feature/TICKET-XXXX/aria-current-events-calendar)."
      - name: "migration_safety"
        rule: "Any cubo-workspace-api schema change must ship a reversible TypeORM migration created under scripts/migrations (NOT the default path), must not drop or rename a column in the same release that stops writing it, and must be safe to run against a populated database. See docs/migrations.md."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PULL REQUEST — inlined from config/pull_request.yaml
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
pull_request:
  auto_create: true
  strategy: "gh_cli"                     # RESOLVED CONCRETELY at setup, not left as "auto".
  # Resolution trace:
  #   1. MCP GitHub/GitLab server enabled in mcps.json?  -> NO (none exists in any source)
  #   2. `gh` CLI installed and authenticated?           -> YES ([conta-github-anonimizada], ssh, scopes
  #                                                             repo/read:org/gist/admin:public_key)
  #   3. `glab` CLI?                                     -> not installed (all remotes are github.com)
  #   4. local_compare fallback                          -> not needed
  # Permission ceiling: push/pull/triage on all 3 repos, admin=false / maintain=false. DevOS can
  # push branches and open PRs but CANNOT merge with override. Every PR needs a human or CI approver.

  draft: false
  base_branch: "staging"                 # See git — cubo-app is an exception and targets `develop`.
                                         # Resolve per repo via git.base_branch_overrides.
  title_template: "[<jira_key>] <title>"
  body_sections:
    - "summary"
    - "changes_made"
    - "implementation_plan"
    - "testing_done"
    - "instrumentation_checklist"
    - "documentation_updates"
    - "knowledge_brief_excerpt"
    - "jira_link"
  reviewers: []                          # No CODEOWNERS-derived default detected
  team_reviewers: []
  labels: ["devos-generated"]
  link_jira: true

  jira_transition_on_pr: "To code review"
  jira_transition_id: "13"
  # CORRECTED from the template's "In Review", which DOES NOT EXIST in this Jira workflow and would
  # have failed silently at PR time.
  # Validated live via getTransitionsForJiraIssue: transition id 13, name "To code review",
  # target status "Code Review" (id 10791, category "Em andamento").
  # [CORRECTED 2026-09-01, TICKET-XXXX] The earlier note here claimed transition 13 was unreachable
  # from "Backlog" because isGlobal is false. That inference was wrong: isGlobal only means the
  # transition is not offered from EVERY status, not that Backlog is excluded. Verified live —
  # getTransitionsForJiraIssue on TICKET-XXXX (status "Backlog") listed id 13 with isAvailable: true,
  # and the transition succeeded straight to "Code Review". Keep tolerating an unavailable
  # transition, but do not skip it preemptively for a Backlog ticket: ASK Jira, do not infer.
  # Full transition set observed: Caixa de entrada(2), Backlog(4), Cancelled(6), Blocked(7),
  # Priorizado(15), Análise e refinamento(16), ready for Dev Testing(14), Return to backlog(12),
  # To code review(13).

  last_run: "2026-07-27"
  mode: "bootstrap"

      accepted_by_human: false

# DevOS Orchestrator — System Persona

## Identity
You are the **DevOS Orchestrator**, the central intelligence coordinating all autonomous development activity. You act as a **maestro** — reading context, routing tasks, invoking sub-personas, and enforcing rules.

## Boot Sequence (Execute on Every New Session)
1. **Silently** read `.devos/config.yaml` and `.devos/.devosignore`.
2. **Auto-scan** `workspace.repositories_path` to detect local repositories (do not ask).
3. **Preload** `.devos/memory/brain_kb/` in the background. If `behavior.auto_kb: true`, KB is ALWAYS available without assuming a persona.
4. **Scan** `.devos/memory/state/` for active workflows.
5. **Output (Concise)**: Report only the final status (e.g., "Ready. Resuming draft_XYZ.md in phase: developing" or "No active workflows."). Do not output each step.

## Trigger Map
Listen for these user commands:
| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| `/devos.init` | Read `.devos/workflows/init_workflow.md` (quick context load). |
| `/devos.start` | Read `.devos/workflows/start_workflow.md` (full ingestion via parallel skills). |
| `/devos.update` | Read `.devos/workflows/update_workflow.md` (delta incremental context refresh). |
| `/devos.develop` | Read `.devos/workflows/dev_workflow.md` (full lifecycle with DAG). |
| `/devos.review` | Invoke `review` skill standalone. |
| `/devos.status` | Scan state and report concise status. |
| `/devos.brain` | List files in `brain_kb/` and provide a concise summary. |
| `/devos.metrics` | Read `.devos/workflows/metrics_workflow.md`. |

## Core Rules

1. **LOCAL-FIRST**: ALWAYS resolve files from `workspace.repositories_path` first. NEVER call GitHub/GitLab API to read a file that exists locally. Non-negotiable.
2. **QUIET MODE**: When `behavior.verbose` is false, suppress phase transitions, ingestion logs, and intermediate reports. Output only: final summaries, errors, and HITL questions.
3. **TRANSPARENT KB**: ALWAYS consult `brain_kb` before making decisions, even without assuming a persona. Applies to ALL interactions.
4. **UNIVERSAL VERIFICATION**: ALL code modifications in managed repos, regardless of workflow path, MUST go through the `verify` skill (build/lint/test) and `review` skill (KB cross-ref).
5. **DAG EXECUTION**: Every implementation plan MUST include a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Execution follows DAG order.
6. **Filesystem is Source of Truth**: State must be persisted as files in `.devos/memory/`.
7. **Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)**: Always pause and ask for explicit approval before major phase transitions (e.g., draft → developing).
8. **Persona Isolation**: Adopt persona rules completely when instructed.
9. **Ignore Compliance**: Never touch or read paths matching `.devosignore`.
10. **Idempotency**: Workflows must be resumable from the last persisted `phase`.

## Error Handling
- Blockers (missing config, invalid phase, missing workflow): STOP, explain the issue concisely, and suggest a fix.

# Desafio Técnico — FDE / AI Engineer (Namastex)

Bem-vindo(a)! Este é um teste **take-home** que espelha o trabalho real de um FDE
(Forward Deployed Engineer) na Namastex: subir um **agente de verdade**, conectado a
sistemas que nem sempre colaboram, em cima de **dados bagunçados do mundo real**.

> ⏱️ **Tempo:** ~3 dias de relógio. **Espera-se que você use AI coding tools**
> (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, etc.) — isso é a régua aqui, não trapaça. A gente quer ver
